subject: Orbitly — capacity pathways, throughput analysis & pricing alternatives
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@orbitly.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orbitly.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity options for high-concurrency QA workloads

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — Orbitly's engineering lead asked me to follow up with concrete sizing and pricing for a Dedicated pool. We're moving the docs search + user-facing QA feature to a 24/7 service and want predictable latency and cost. Quick summary of our workload (attached CSV includes sample traces):
- Peak request rate: ~55 reqs/sec (5-minute peak)
- Sustained average: ~22 reqs/sec
- Avg input size: 1,200 tokens; avg output: 350 tokens
- Typical context pinned at ~3,072 tokens (we include user history + doc chunk)
- Concurrency objective: support ~40 simultaneous interactive sessions with p95 latency under 800ms for generation
- Model profile: we expect to use a 16B dense open model (your catalog) with KV cache support and streaming responses

Can you recommend: 1) a committed GPU pool size, 2) throughput guarantees / SLOs we should expect, and 3) monthly committed pricing (we're exploring 6- vs 12-month commits). Also flag any packaging/feature constraints (bursting, warm KV cache, autoscale).

Appreciate a clear table of options — we need this for procurement.

Best,
Anika
Anika Shah
Head of Product, Orbitly
anika.shah@orbitly.ai

Attachment: Orbitly-workload-metrics-202610.csv (CSV, 42 KB)

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, procurement@orbitly.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for high-concurrency QA workloads

Hi Anika — thanks for the detail and the trace file, that helps a lot. High-level recommendation below; I'll follow up with a concise pricing table and a short internal note to confirm engineering assumptions. TL;DR: 6-GPU committed pool (A100-80GB class equivalent) with a 12-month commit gives the best trade-off for your profile.

Sizing rationale (quick):
- Token throughput: given avg request (~1,550 tokens total round-trip) and 55 req/s peaks, raw token load at peak ~85k tokens/sec. With Redwood batching + KV cache on user session prefixes, we conservatively assume ~2.8x efficiency (prefix caching + batching reduces duplicate compute).
- Per-GPU sustained generation capacity (16B baseline with our optimized kernels): ~14k tokens/sec (sustained) per A100-80GB equivalent for mixed gen/kv workloads.
- Effective pool capacity: 6 GPUs * 14k = ~84k tokens/sec sustained — matches your observed peak after cache factors.
- Concurrency: that size supports ~40 interactive sessions with p95 generation latency ~400–700ms depending on request overlap and streaming policy. We can target p95 < 800ms out of the box; p95 < 500ms is achievable with additional capacity or stricter batching knobs.

Operational notes / packaging:
- Warm KV cache: we recommend session pinning to pool nodes for users with heavy history (configurable) — this materially improves tail latency.
- Bursting: committed pool + burst capacity available (adds transient GPUs) for traffic spikes — typical burst headroom we offer is +50% of committed capacity at higher overage rate.
- Autoscale: you can set min=6 committed, max=12 (burst) with policy-driven fallbacks to a lighter quantized model if needed.

Proposed commercial options (overview):
A) 6-GPU committed, 12 months — recommended (stable pricing, most predictable)
B) 6-GPU committed, 6 months — slightly higher price per GPU (shorter commit)
C) 4-GPU committed, 12 months + automated burst to 8 GPUs — lower base cost but higher risk of p95 latency increases during sustained peaks

I'll pull together a short pricing matrix and candidate discount tiers. Looping in Marissa for throughput validation and Ben on packaging/pricing mechanics.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orbitly — capacity pathways, throughput analysis & pricing alternatives

Quick engineering check after scanning the traces and a micro-bench:
- Bench confirms ~13–15k tokens/sec sustained on A100-80GB equiv for that 16B model with our runtime flags (continuous batching enabled, int8 quant path for matmuls).
- If Orbitly expects heavy session stickiness (many repeated prefixes), we get better than 2.8x cache efficiency — could be 3.5x in top decile; but plan conservatively at 2.8x for procurement.
- Warmup time for KV cache per user ~200–600ms depending on context length; recommend 60s session pinning for interactive UX.
- For p95 < 500ms target, suggest recommending a 8-GPU committed baseline or 6-GPU + guaranteed burst of 2 GPUs during business hours (we can SLA the burst eligibility in the contract).

I'll sign off on the 6-GPU baseline numbers; price decks need to reflect optional upsell to 8 GPUs for latency-sensitive SLAs.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Orbitly — capacity pathways, throughput analysis & pricing alternatives

Hi Anika — attached is a concise proposal with three commercial paths (short table included below). I've baked in Marissa's confirmation and included an explicit burst SLA option. If you'd like, we can spin up a one-week smoke test on a small dedicated pool (metered) before sign.

Commercial summary (monthly committed cost, illustrative):
- Option 1 (Recommended): 6-GPU committed (A100-80GB class) — baseline capacity; expected p95 ~400–700ms; monthly committed price: $105,000/mo (12-month commit). 15% discount vs list for 12-month.
- Option 2: 6-GPU committed (6-month) — $115,000/mo (shorter term, no extra credits). 8% discount vs list.
- Option 3: 4-GPU committed + burst to 8 (12-month) — $78,500/mo + burst overage at $X/hr when used; recommended only if you want lower committed spend and can tolerate higher tail latency.

Add-ons:
- Burst SLA (guaranteed availability of +2 GPUs during 9a–6p PST on weekdays) — $6,500/mo.
- Extended observability retention (token-level traces + 90-day eval history) — $2,800/mo.
- Initial 1-week smoke test on a 2-GPU pool (metered to your account) — no cost, we only bill overages if you exceed the test cap.

Next steps: 1) Confirm preferred option + commit term, 2) Procurement sends PO or requests SOW, 3) We provide DocuSign + onboarding runbook and schedule a kickoff with Marissa for runtime knobs.

I've attached the short proposal PDF and a DocuSign link; happy to jump on a call tomorrow.

— Vivek

Vivek — thanks, this is the clearest layout we've seen so far. A few procurement questions before we loop finance: 
1) Can Orbitly get a 30-day ramp (start with 2 GPUs and scale to committed in 30 days) instead of an immediate start?
2) Any chance of an additional 3% one-time sign-up credit for case-specific onboarding efforts (we have an internal SSO + custom routing to integrate)?
3) Billing cadence: monthly in arrears vs quarterly invoicing options?

If you can confirm 1–3, procurement will be comfortable taking the proposal to finance for approval. Also — we prefer a 12-month committed term but want the ramp flexibility.

Thanks,
Anika

Head of Product, Orbitly

Hi Anika — great questions. Short answers: 1) Yes — we can do a 30-day ramp (2 GPUs initial, scale to committed size by day 30) and we'll provide a runbook to manage warm cache during ramp. 2) We can offer a one-time 3% onboarding credit for SSO + routing integration (applied to first invoice). 3) Billing: default is monthly in arrears; we can provide quarterly invoicing with net-30 payment terms (requires minor contracting addendum).

I'll update the DocuSign SOW to reflect the 30-day ramp and the 3% onboarding credit and circulate a revised commercial term sheet. If procurement is good with quarterly billing, we'll mark that in the payment terms.

If you're OK, I'll send the updated SOW today and loop in our legal ops to speed DocuSign.

— Vivek
